review: The Arabic opens each stanza with the imperative احْفَظْ ('guard/keep'), five times over; the Hebrew keeps the same anaphora with שְׁמֹר, which is the hymn's whole device.
4:2 לֹא לִי חֶפְצִי עוֹד — the Arabic لَيْسَ مُرَادِي الْآنَ لِي is 'my wish is no longer mine'; the Hebrew keeps the verbless negation and the dative לִי, so the line reads as the surrender it is.
4:3–4:4 קָנוּי — the Arabic فَيُمْتَلَك is 'that it be possessed'; the glossary verb קָנָה keeps the sense of acquisition (Exod 15:16, קָנִיתָ), which is stronger than a bare 'belonging'.

2:4 בְּאָרְחוֹתֶיךָ הַיְשָׁרוֹת — the Arabic سُلُوكِ طُرْقِكَ الْقَوِيم is 'walking Your upright paths'; אֹרַח is the poetic path (Ps 25:4) and יָשָׁר the adjective of the same psalm, so the verse's vocabulary is kept.
5:1 צְפוּנָה — the Arabic ذَاخِرًا is 'storing up'; צָפַן is the biblical verb for laying up treasure (Prov 2:7), and the feminine agrees with אַהֲבָה so the line stays one image.
